text: The concentration of aqueous chloride ions can be found by titration with aqueous silver nitrate,
The indicator used is aqueous potassium chromate(VI), K CrO (aq).
As AgNO (aq) is added to aqueous chloride ions, a white precipitate of AgCl(s) is formed.
When all the chloride ions have reacted, further addition of AgNO (aq) leads to the formation of
a red precipitate of silver chromate(VI), Ag CrO (s). The first appearance of the red precipitate
shows the end-point of the titration.

2 Effusion is the process in which a gas escapes through a small hole.
A student investigates the relationship between rate of effusion and relative molar mass of a gas
using the apparatus shown in Fig. 2.1.
plunger
gas syringe
gas being tested
side-arm tube
three-way tap
aluminium foil with small hole
Fig. 2.1
The following method is used:
step 1 Turn the tap and remove any gas from the syringe through the side-arm tube, by pushing
in the plunger.
step 2 Add 50 cm of the gas being tested to the syringe through the side-arm tube.
step 3 Remove the gas from the syringe, through the side-arm tube, by pushing in the plunger.
step 4 Add 70 cm of the gas being tested to the syringe through the side-arm tube.
step 5 Turn the tap to connect the syringe to the tube with the aluminium foil and small hole.
step 6 Allow the syringe plunger to fall and start a timer when the volume of gas in the syringe
reaches 60 cm .
step 7 Stop the timer when the volume of gas in the syringe reaches 10 cm . Record the time
taken.
step 8 Repeat steps 1 to 7 with different gases.
